minor_characters.name: Director of Companies (frame host on the Nellie)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Introduces the frame scene on the Thames in Ch 001 and reappears only to note the ebb at the very end of Ch 003.
minor_characters.reason_removable: His specific identity and traits are not needed for the frame to function; the yawl and anonymous listeners suffice to preserve the opening/closing shape in the synopsis.

minor_characters.name: The Lawyer (on the Nellie)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A silent listener on the yacht in Ch 001 who never affects Marlow’s tale.
minor_characters.reason_removable: He is mere scene-dressing in the frame and can be elided without loss to plot, theme, or character.

minor_characters.name: The Accountant (on the Nellie, frame figure)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Another silent listener in Ch 001 distinct from the Company’s chief accountant ashore.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Removing this frame extra avoids confusion with the indispensable chief accountant at the Outer Station and changes nothing substantive.

minor_characters.name: Van Shuyten
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A Dutch outfitter mentioned only in the Russian’s backstory in Ch 002–003.
minor_characters.reason_removable: He exists solely to color the Russian’s past and has no bearing on Marlow, Kurtz, or the plot.

minor_characters.name: Towson (Towser), author of the seamanship manual
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Named on the cover of the old nautical book found at the riverside hut in Ch 002.
minor_characters.reason_removable: The scene’s function (a cipher-annotated manual signaling another white man) is fully preserved without naming its long-dead author.

subplots.name: Marlow’s fainting trek companion and the hammock fiasco
subplots.reason_removable: This comic-miserable side episode during the 200‑mile march neither advances the plot nor adds insight beyond the already ample trek brutality.

subplots.name: The boiler-maker friendship, pigeon‑fancying, and moonlit jig for rivets
subplots.reason_removable: These amiable asides can be compressed to ‘foreman helps repair the boat’ without affecting the rivet‑delay arc central to the chapter.

subplots.name: The camp’s nightly hunt for a ‘charmed’ hippopotamus
subplots.reason_removable: This running joke exists as local color and does not influence the steamer repair, the Manager conflict, or Marlow’s fixation on Kurtz.

subplots.name: The Russian’s life story (runaway sailor, arch‑priest’s son, Dutch outfitter)
subplots.reason_removable: His zealous loyalty to Kurtz can be conveyed in a line or two without the multi‑paragraph personal history that never returns.

digressions.topic: Roll‑call of English navigators and ships on the Thames (Drake, Franklin, Golden Hind, Erebus and Terror).
digressions.reason_removable: Name‑checking this historical catalog adds atmosphere but the frame’s imperial irony and the ‘dark places of the earth’ point stand without it.

digressions.topic: General essay on ‘seamen’s minds’ versus Marlow’s notion that a tale’s meaning lies ‘outside’.
digressions.reason_removable: This meta‑narrative musing is stylistically signature but nonessential to following the plot or the synopsis’s thematic throughline.

digressions.topic: Vermouth interlude with the shabby clerk and his ‘quoth Plato’ quip before the doctor visit.
digressions.reason_removable: It is pure comic filler around the indispensable doctor scene and can be lifted without loss.

digressions.topic: Extended portrait of the boiler‑maker’s beard‑wrapper, laundry routine, and pigeon lore.
digressions.reason_removable: These charming details are expendable local color that do not alter events or character arcs.

digressions.topic: Road‑overseer vignette and the bullet‑holed corpse as ‘permanent improvement’ during the inland march.
digressions.reason_removable: The Outer Station’s grove of dying helpers already establishes colonial brutality, making this extra tableau redundant for the abridgment.

digressions.topic: Technical inventory of the steamer’s layout and pilot‑house furniture.
digressions.reason_removable: The mechanics of the deck scow are immaterial to the river journey’s action and mood preserved in the synopsis.

digressions.topic: Manager’s round‑table anecdote and the note on his coast ‘boy’s’ insolence.
digressions.reason_removable: These side notes reinforce pettiness already evident elsewhere and can be pruned without affecting the ‘unsound method’ throughline.

digressions.topic: Marlow’s aside about a Scotch sailmaker certain of inhabitants on Mars.
digressions.reason_removable: It is a whimsical aside that neither shapes the action nor deepens any principal character.

digressions.topic: Inventory‑like description of the Intended’s drawing‑room furnishings (piano as sarcophagus, gilt legs, marble fireplace).
digressions.reason_removable: The core scene—Marlow’s lie and her preserving illusion—remains intact without the furniture catalog.
